chunks: What will you do with the vastness of this house in this world, when you are in greater need of it in the Hereafter?

Yes, if you wish, you can take it to the Hereafter: by entertaining guests in it, maintaining kinship ties in it, and discharging obligations at their due times; thus you will have taken it to the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: How can worldly wealth be converted into spiritual reward for the Hereafter according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this reflection from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the attachment to worldly luxury by urging the companion to view his expansive house as a means of *sadaqah* (charity) rather than mere comfort. He outlines three specific mechanisms for this spiritual conversion: *iqrāʾ al-ḍayf* (hospitality), *ṣilat al-raḥim* (maintaining kinship ties), and *iṭlāʾ al-ḥuqūq* (discharging rights), thereby transforming material wealth into eternal merit. This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on the practical application of wealth in social welfare as a direct pathway to the Hereafter.
